item.content:encoded:
The AFS Youth Assembly is inviting its alumni to apply to become Impact Coordinators, a significant global leadership opportunity designed for young changemakers who want to help transform ideas into measurable social impact while strengthening youth-led initiatives across different regions of the world.

Launched as part of the next phase of the AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network, the Impact Coordinator opportunity places selected alumni at the center of regional youth engagement, project development, mentorship, collaboration, and impact-building. Impact Coordinators will serve for a two-year term, working with Youth Assembly alumni in their respective regions and helping them develop ideas, identify resources, connect with relevant opportunities, and advance projects that contribute to positive social change.

A particularly attractive benefit of the opportunity is that selected Impact Coordinators will receive a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, Switzerland. Coordinators will also receive training support and an AFS Global Competence Certificate while developing practical leadership, communication, organizational, mentoring, networking, and project coordination skills.

About the AFS Youth Assembly

The AFS Youth Assembly is an international platform that brings together young leaders, changemakers, social entrepreneurs, activists, students, professionals, educators, and other individuals committed to building more inclusive, peaceful, sustainable, and equitable societies.

The platform focuses on helping emerging leaders connect across borders, develop global competence, acquire practical skills, build partnerships, and translate ideas into action.

The Youth Assembly was founded in 2004 by the Friendship Ambassadors Foundation and is now part of AFS Intercultural Programs. AFS is an international nonprofit organization focused on intercultural learning and the development of knowledge, skills, and understanding that can contribute to a more just and peaceful world.

The Youth Assembly is intended to be more than a stand-alone international gathering. Participants are encouraged to continue their development and community engagement after attending the Assembly through opportunities such as the Alumni Impact Network, leadership roles, mentoring, project development, collaboration, and other AFS activities.

What Is the AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network?

The AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network is a global community created to help former Youth Assembly participants continue developing their ideas and generating impact after the Assembly.

Rather than allowing the Youth Assembly experience to end when delegates return home, the network provides a structure through which alumni can remain connected, collaborate with other changemakers, obtain mentorship, access useful resources, develop their skills, pursue project support, and showcase their achievements.

The network is designed to support alumni in several important areas, including:

  • Developing and implementing action-oriented projects;
  • Receiving mentorship and connections to relevant experts;
  • Accessing opportunities for seed funding;
  • Building regional and international partnerships;
  • Connecting with other Youth Assembly alumni;
  • Showcasing successful projects and achievements internationally;
  • Participating in skills-development activities; and
  • Receiving peer-to-peer support from other young changemakers.

The Alumni Impact Network is open to people who have previously participated in a session of the Youth Assembly.

Why AFS Is Recruiting Impact Coordinators

Following the 31st AFS Youth Assembly held in Geneva in August 2026, the Alumni Impact Network is moving into another stage of its development.

AFS is coordinating alumni engagement and impact activities across six major geographic regions:

  1. Africa
  2. Asia and Oceania
  3. Europe
  4. Latin America and the Caribbean
  5. Middle East and North Africa
  6. North America

Impact Coordinators are intended to provide the regional leadership needed to connect alumni, encourage collaboration and help turn promising ideas into practical initiatives.

They will effectively serve as an important connection between the wider AFS Youth Assembly network and alumni working on projects and initiatives within their regions.

What Does an AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Do?

An Impact Coordinator is expected to be more than a representative or titleholder. The position involves actively engaging with Youth Assembly alumni and helping create an environment where ideas, partnerships, resources, mentorship, and youth-led action can come together.

Coordinators will help alumni progress from having an idea to developing and implementing meaningful activities.

Their work can involve motivating alumni, connecting changemakers with one another, identifying useful resources, helping projects gain visibility and keeping AFS informed about the progress being made within their region.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to applicants who already have practical experience in youth engagement, social entrepreneurship, community projects, mentoring, sustainable development, advocacy, nonprofit activities or other forms of social impact.

Key Responsibilities of an Impact Coordinator

Selected Impact Coordinators will take on several major responsibilities during their two-year leadership term.

1. Provide Regional Leadership

Impact Coordinators will help organize and mobilize Youth Assembly alumni within the region they represent.

This requires maintaining engagement among alumni rather than simply communicating with them occasionally. Coordinators should be capable of encouraging participation, building relationships and creating a stronger regional community of changemakers.

2. Organize Alumni Engagement Activities

Coordinators are expected to bring alumni together through regular engagement.

Depending on circumstances, this may include:

  • Virtual meetings;
  • In-person gatherings;
  • Networking activities;
  • Collaborative discussions;
  • Project-focused sessions; and
  • Other opportunities that encourage alumni to work together.

The broader purpose is to create meaningful collaboration rather than allowing alumni projects to operate entirely in isolation.

3. Help Alumni Turn Ideas into Action

An important part of the position involves supporting alumni who have ideas for social-impact projects or initiatives.

Impact Coordinators should understand how ideas can be developed into practical projects and should be able to help other young changemakers move through this process.

This is one reason AFS is specifically looking for candidates who understand project ideation and who have previously started or participated in successful projects, initiatives or social ventures.

4. Provide Mentorship and Support

Impact Coordinators will have an important mentoring function.

They will help Youth Assembly alumni navigate the challenges involved in developing projects and generating social impact. Candidates with previous mentoring experience or experience working directly with young people are therefore particularly relevant to the role.

5. Connect Alumni with Resources

Successful social-impact initiatives often require more than a good idea. They may require partnerships, mentorship, technical knowledge, networks, visibility or financial resources.

Impact Coordinators are therefore expected to understand the youth and social-impact ecosystem and have knowledge of useful resources such as:

  • Impact hubs;
  • Youth networks;
  • Potential partners;
  • Mentors;
  • Relevant organizations;
  • Project-development resources; and
  • Other opportunities that could assist alumni.

The wider Alumni Impact Network itself is designed to connect participants with support mechanisms that include mentorship, expert connections and opportunities for seed funding.

6. Encourage Collaboration

Another major responsibility will be connecting Youth Assembly alumni with one another.

Instead of individual changemakers working separately on similar problems, the network aims to encourage cooperation, knowledge sharing and partnerships.

Strong coordinators should therefore be comfortable bringing people together, facilitating communication and encouraging collaborative action.

7. Track Projects and Progress

Impact Coordinators will also help monitor the progress of projects being implemented or supported within their regions.

They will communicate relevant updates to AFS staff, helping the organization understand how alumni projects and initiatives are progressing.

For candidates interested in international development, project management, monitoring, community engagement or nonprofit leadership, this responsibility provides particularly useful practical experience.

8. Promote Alumni Projects Globally

Successful initiatives should not remain invisible.

Impact Coordinators will help showcase the projects and achievements of Youth Assembly alumni to a wider international audience.

This can increase recognition for youth-led initiatives while allowing successful ideas, experiences and lessons to reach other members of the international AFS community.

Benefits of Becoming an AFS Impact Coordinator

Although the Impact Coordinator position is a volunteer role, it comes with substantial professional-development, leadership and networking benefits.

Full Scholarship to the 2027 Youth Assembly in Geneva

One of the most significant benefits is a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, Switzerland.

This gives selected coordinators the opportunity to return to the international Youth Assembly environment while continuing their leadership journey within the AFS community.

Two Years of Global Leadership Experience

Selected candidates will serve as Impact Coordinators for two years.

A two-year term provides considerably more opportunity to build meaningful relationships, support projects and demonstrate sustained leadership than a short-term volunteer assignment.

International Recognition

Impact Coordinators and the projects they facilitate may be highlighted through social networks and other AFS visibility channels.

This can help coordinators demonstrate their contributions to social impact while increasing the visibility of the initiatives they support.

Leadership and Professional Skills Development

The position provides opportunities to practice skills that can be valuable in future academic and professional settings, including:

  • Leadership;
  • Project coordination;
  • Mentoring;
  • Community building;
  • Stakeholder engagement;
  • Communication;
  • Networking;
  • Organization;
  • Teamwork;
  • Independent working;
  • Project monitoring; and
  • Social-impact development.

AFS Global Competence Certificate

Impact Coordinators will receive an AFS Global Competence Certificate, together with additional training support.

The experience can therefore provide both practical leadership exposure and structured professional development.

Access to a Global Changemaker Community

Impact Coordinators will operate within an established international community of Youth Assembly alumni and changemakers.

The Alumni Impact Network exists specifically to encourage regional and international collaboration, mentorship, project development, access to resources and opportunities for alumni to increase their impact.

Eligibility Requirements for the Impact Coordinator Opportunity

Applicants should review the requirements carefully because this opportunity is not open to the general public.

The most important eligibility requirement is previous participation in the AFS Youth Assembly.

Previous AFS Youth Assembly Participation Is Mandatory

Applicants must have previously attended the AFS Youth Assembly.

AFS explicitly states that the Impact Coordinator position is open only to Youth Assembly alumni. Therefore, someone with excellent leadership or social-impact experience who has never attended the Youth Assembly would not satisfy this fundamental requirement.

Applicants Must Live in the Region They Want to Represent

Candidates must currently live in the geographic region for which they want to serve as an Impact Coordinator.

The six regions covered by the initiative are Africa, Asia and Oceania, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, Middle East and North Africa, and North America.

Strong Interest in Social Impact and the SDGs

Applicants should demonstrate a genuine commitment to social impact and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

This is central to the wider mission of the Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network, which seeks to translate youth leadership into practical action addressing social, environmental and development challenges.

Experience Working with Young People

AFS is seeking applicants with experience working with youth.

Relevant experience could include areas such as mentoring young people or participating in the creation and implementation of action-oriented projects.

Project or Social Venture Experience

Applicants should have started or participated in a successful:

  • Project;
  • Initiative; or
  • Social venture.

This requirement reflects the practical nature of the coordinator role. Candidates will be helping other alumni develop their own initiatives, making previous firsthand project experience particularly valuable.

Understanding of Project Ideation

Candidates should have strong knowledge of the ideation process and understand how social projects and ventures are developed.

This can help coordinators guide alumni from identifying a problem or opportunity through to shaping and advancing a workable initiative.

Networks and Knowledge of Resources

Applicants should have useful connections or knowledge of resources relevant to social-impact work.

These may include impact hubs, organizations, youth resources, partners and other networks that could help Youth Assembly alumni move their projects forward.

Leadership and Communication Skills

AFS is looking for candidates who can demonstrate strong:

  • Leadership skills;
  • Communication skills;
  • Coordination skills; and
  • Organizational abilities.

These competencies are particularly important because coordinators will be responsible for bringing together people from different backgrounds and supporting multiple activities and initiatives.

Ability to Work Independently and Collaboratively

Candidates should be capable of managing responsibilities independently while also working effectively as part of a wider international network.

Computer and Internet Access

Applicants must have personal access to:

  • A computer; and
  • Stable internet connectivity.

This is particularly important because regional and international coordination may involve substantial online communication and virtual engagement.

Time Commitment

Applicants must be willing and able to dedicate sufficient time and effort to the role throughout the appointment.

Potential candidates should therefore consider whether they can realistically maintain an active leadership commitment alongside their academic, professional and personal responsibilities.

English Language Proficiency

Candidates must be proficient in written and spoken English.

Because the position operates within an international network, effective English communication is an important requirement.

Social Media Skills

Applicants should also be comfortable using social media and digital tools for communication and networking.

This aligns with the coordinator’s responsibility to connect alumni and help promote youth-led projects and achievements.

Connection to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals

The Impact Coordinator initiative has a strong relationship with the Sustainable Development Goals.

The AFS Youth Assembly Alumni Impact Network is built around supporting youth-led action on major global and regional challenges. The Declaration of Impact 2026, launched during the 31st AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva, establishes shared global and regional priorities and emphasizes collaboration, inclusion, education, equality, sustainability, innovation, health and well-being, and youth leadership.

Impact Coordinators can therefore play an important role in helping young changemakers translate broad sustainable-development ambitions into practical regional and community-level initiatives.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity is particularly suitable for eligible Youth Assembly alumni who see themselves as facilitators and community builders rather than individuals interested only in adding another title to their résumé.

Strong potential applicants are likely to be people who enjoy:

  • Helping other young leaders succeed;
  • Mentoring and advising peers;
  • Developing social-impact projects;
  • Building partnerships;
  • Organizing communities and networks;
  • Connecting people with resources;
  • Promoting youth-led initiatives;
  • Working toward the Sustainable Development Goals;
  • Communicating across cultures; and
  • Taking responsibility for long-term initiatives.

Applicants should also be prepared for the reality that this is an active two-year volunteer commitment rather than a passive honorary position.

Application Deadline

No application deadline is stated in the official AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator announcement.

Because the official announcement provides an application link without publishing a closing date, interested and eligible Youth Assembly alumni should check the current application status and consider submitting their application as early as possible rather than assuming that applications will remain open indefinitely.

How to Apply for the AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Opportunity

Eligible applicants should complete the official Impact Coordinator application provided by the AFS Youth Assembly.

Before applying, candidates should ensure that they:

  1. Have previously participated in the AFS Youth Assembly;
  2. Currently live in the region they intend to represent;
  3. Can demonstrate youth engagement or mentoring experience;
  4. Have relevant experience with projects, initiatives or social ventures;
  5. Understand social-project development and ideation;
  6. Can demonstrate leadership, communication, coordination and organizational abilities;
  7. Have sufficient time to commit to the two-year role;
  8. Have reliable access to a computer and stable internet;
  9. Are proficient in spoken and written English; and
  10. Are comfortable using social media and online networking tools.

Official AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator Announcement and Application

Why This Opportunity Matters

The AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator opportunity provides alumni with a chance to move from participating in an international youth platform to helping shape what happens after delegates return to their communities.

The role is particularly significant because it focuses on the stage where many promising youth initiatives face their greatest challenge: converting enthusiasm and ideas into sustained action.

By connecting alumni with mentorship, resources, partnerships, collaboration and wider visibility, Impact Coordinators can help create stronger regional ecosystems for youth-led change.

For the coordinators themselves, the opportunity combines practical leadership experience, international networking, skills development, global recognition, training support and a full scholarship to attend the 2027 Youth Assembly in Geneva.

Conclusion

The AFS Youth Assembly Impact Coordinator 2026 opportunity is an attractive international leadership opportunity for Youth Assembly alumni who have demonstrated commitment to youth empowerment, social impact and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Selected coordinators will undertake a two-year volunteer leadership role, helping organize and motivate alumni, support youth-led projects, connect changemakers with useful resources, encourage collaboration, monitor project progress and increase the global visibility of alumni initiatives.

In return, coordinators can gain significant leadership and professional-development experience, receive training support and an AFS Global Competence Certificate, strengthen their international networks, gain recognition for their contributions and receive a full scholarship to attend the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly in Geneva.

However, prospective applicants should pay particular attention to the principal eligibility condition: only previous Youth Assembly participants are eligible to become Impact Coordinators.

Since no closing date is currently stated in the official announcement, eligible alumni interested in the opportunity should review the official application information and apply promptly.

item.content:encoded:
Dreaming of an international career with purpose?

The United Nations Young Professionals Programme (YPP) offers talented and highly qualified young professionals an opportunity to begin a career as an international civil servant with the United Nations Secretariat. 🌍🇺🇳

Applications are expected to open in mid-October — but you do not need to wait until applications open to start preparing.

If you are considering applying, now is the time to check your eligibility, understand the application requirements and begin preparing for the YPP examination.

Read on to learn about the UN YPP, eligibility requirements, application process, examination stages and how to prepare.

What Is the United Nations Young Professionals Programme (YPP)?

Young Professionals Programme

The UN Young Professionals Programme (YPP) is a recruitment initiative for talented, highly qualified professionals to start a career as an international civil servant with the UN Secretariat. It consists of an entrance examination process and professional development once those who are successful start their career with the UN.

The YPP examination is held once a year in different subject areas, depending on the needs of the UN. YPP is open to nationals of participating countries. The list of participating countries varies from year to year. The application period typically opens in June each year.

Applications Open Mid-October — Start Preparing Now

If you are interested in applying for the YPP, do not wait until the application window opens to begin preparing.

Applications are expected to open in mid-October, making this the ideal time to:

  • Check whether your country is participating.
  • Confirm that you meet the age and education requirements.
  • Check your English or French language proficiency.
  • Review the YPP application requirements.
  • Gather your degree and identification documents.
  • Update your CV and employment information.
  • Familiarise yourself with the examination format.
  • Begin reviewing relevant preparation materials.
  • Make sure you understand the subject area for the upcoming examination.

The application process itself is only one part of the journey. Candidates should also allow enough time to prepare for the competitive YPP examination.

Start preparing now so that you are ready when applications open.

Who Can Apply for the UN Young Professionals Programme?

To be eligible for the YPP, candidates generally need to meet the following requirements.

1. Nationality

You must be a national of a participating United Nations Member State.

The participating countries are not necessarily the same every year, so applicants should check the official YPP announcement for the relevant examination cycle.

2. Education

You must have at least a first-level university degree relevant to the examination subject area.

This generally means having a relevant Bachelor’s degree or a three-year equivalent first university degree.

3. Age

Candidates must be 32 years old or younger in the year of the examination.

The specific birth-date requirement should always be checked against the official announcement for the relevant YPP cycle.

4. Language

Candidates must be fluent in English or French, which are the two working languages used for the YPP examination.

How to Apply for the UN YPP

YPP applications are submitted online through the United Nations recruitment system, Inspira.

Before applying, candidates should:

  1. Confirm that their nationality is included among the participating countries.
  2. Check the age requirement.
  3. Confirm that their university degree is relevant to the examination subject.
  4. Confirm their English or French language proficiency.
  5. Review the specific YPP job opening.
  6. Prepare the required documentation.
  7. Complete and submit the online application before the deadline.

Applications are normally submitted through the relevant YPP job opening on the UN Careers/Inspira platform.

What Happens After You Apply?

Applications are screened to determine whether candidates meet the basic eligibility requirements.

The screening process considers factors including:

  • Nationality
  • Age
  • Education
  • Language proficiency

If there are more than 90 eligible applicants from the same country for a particular examination area, additional criteria may be used to rank candidates.

These can include:

  • Highest level of education
  • Knowledge of additional official UN languages
  • Relevant professional experience

Where the examination has two stages, candidates may be selected for the first stage based on this ranking, with a smaller number progressing to the second stage.

Applicants are informed of the outcome of the screening process.

UN YPP Application Timeline

*The timeline can change from year to year.

For the upcoming application cycle, candidates should prepare ahead of the expected mid-October opening rather than waiting until applications go live.

How to Prepare for the UN YPP Application

Preparation should begin before the application deadline.

Check your eligibility early

Do not leave it until the last minute to discover that you do not meet an eligibility requirement.

Check:

  • Your nationality
  • Your age
  • Your degree
  • Your language proficiency
  • The examination subject area

Prepare your documents

You may need documentation confirming your identity, nationality and education.

Make sure your documents are available and that the information in your application is accurate and consistent.

Review your education information

When completing your application, provide accurate information about your university degree.

If there are differences between your degree and the terminology used in the application system, use the appropriate section to explain them rather than selecting an inaccurate option.

Check your language proficiency carefully

Language proficiency is important.

Candidates must demonstrate fluency in either English or French. The UN application process considers speaking, reading, writing and understanding.

Anything below the required level of fluency in one of these areas can affect eligibility.

What Is the UN YPP Examination Like?

The YPP examination normally consists of an online examination, often conducted in two stages, followed by an interview for candidates who progress through the process.

Candidates can use the UN’s examination preparation resources to familiarise themselves with the format and expectations.

Preparation materials can include:

  • Reading lists
  • Sample questions
  • Previous examination questions
  • Examination tips and guidance

Stage One: General and Specialized Questions

The first stage normally consists of multiple-choice questions covering both:

General assessment

This may assess areas such as:

  • Written communication
  • Reasoning
  • UN core values
  • UN competencies

Specialized assessment

This focuses on knowledge relevant to the specific YPP examination subject area.

The first stage generally lasts around two hours and is conducted in English or French.

Stage Two: Specialized Examination

Candidates who progress to the second stage may complete a more detailed specialized examination.

This stage can include constructed or open-ended questions related to the examination subject.

The examination generally lasts approximately two to two and a half hours.

Some questions may allow candidates to respond in one of the six official UN languages, depending on the examination requirements.

Candidates should pay close attention to:

  • Question instructions
  • Word limits
  • Time management
  • The specific requirements of each question

The examination may also be remotely proctored.

YPP Interview

Candidates who successfully progress through the examination stages may be invited to a competency-based interview, generally conducted by video conference.

The interview provides an opportunity to demonstrate relevant competencies and suitability for a career with the United Nations.

Candidates should therefore prepare examples that demonstrate their skills, experience, judgement and ability to work effectively in an international environment.

How Competitive Is the UN YPP?

The YPP is a competitive recruitment programme.

The number of candidates who can progress through the screening and examination stages may depend on the number of eligible applicants from each participating country and the examination subject area.

This makes early preparation particularly important.

Being eligible does not guarantee selection, and passing an examination does not automatically mean that a candidate will be offered a position.

What Happens If You Pass the YPP Examination?

Successful candidates may be placed on a YPP roster for suitable vacancies.

The roster is generally valid for three years.

However, being placed on the roster does not guarantee employment with the United Nations.

Candidates selected for positions may be offered a two-year fixed-term appointment, with the possibility of continuing employment subject to satisfactory performance and applicable UN policies.

What Grade Do YPP Candidates Receive?

Depending on their qualifications and experience, successful candidates may enter at the:

P-1 level

Generally applicable to candidates with a Bachelor’s degree and no relevant professional work experience.

P-2 level

Generally applicable to candidates with:

  • A Bachelor’s degree and two years of relevant work experience, or
  • A Master’s degree and no relevant work experience.

Candidates are generally expected to spend at least two years in their first position.

Where Can UN YPP Candidates Be Posted?

YPP professionals may be assigned to different United Nations duty stations depending on organisational needs.

Possible locations include:

  • Addis Ababa
  • Bangkok
  • Beirut
  • Geneva
  • Nairobi
  • New York
  • Santiago
  • Vienna

Candidates should be prepared to serve at different duty stations and, where applicable, in field operations.

Managed Reassignment Programme

After serving in their initial position for at least two years, eligible staff may participate in the Managed Reassignment Programme.

The programme is intended to support professional development, diversify staff experience and help employees develop skills through different assignments.

Upcoming UN YPP Examination Subject

The examination subject area changes according to the staffing needs of the United Nations.

For the relevant cycle, applicants should carefully review the official YPP announcement to confirm:

  • The examination subject
  • Participating countries
  • Eligibility requirements
  • Application dates
  • Examination dates
  • Required qualifications

This information can change from one cycle to another.

UN Staff and the Young Professionals Programme

Current United Nations staff may also be eligible to participate in the YPP under specific internal arrangements.

Staff members in General Service and related categories, as well as certain Field Service staff, may be eligible depending on their grade, appointment, nationality, qualifications, performance and other requirements.

There are also specific provisions for internal candidates progressing from General Service positions to professional positions.

Employees interested in this route should check the relevant internal YPP vacancy and eligibility requirements in Inspira.

Check the official UN YPP information and prepare ahead of the application opening.

Beware of Companies Charging for YPP Applications

Applicants should be cautious of companies that charge fees for YPP-related services.

The United Nations has stated that it does not collaborate or partner with for-profit companies offering YPP application or examination services.

There are no fees for submitting a YPP application, taking the examination or undergoing the evaluation process.

Candidates can access official information and preparation materials publicly and free of charge.

Frequently Asked Questions About the UN YPP

When will UN YPP applications open?

Applications for the upcoming cycle are expected to open in mid-October. Candidates should monitor the official UN Careers/Inspira announcement for the exact opening and closing dates.

Can I start preparing before applications open?

Yes — and you should.

Use the period before applications open to check your eligibility, gather your documents, understand the examination format and begin studying the relevant subject area.

What age do I need to be?

Candidates generally need to be 32 years old or younger in the year of the examination. Always check the exact requirement in the official announcement.

Do I need a Master’s degree?

No. A relevant first-level university degree, such as a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent, can meet the education requirement.

Do I need work experience?

Work experience is not necessarily an eligibility requirement. However, relevant professional experience can be considered when ranking candidates where there are large numbers of eligible applicants.

Which languages are accepted?

Candidates must generally be fluent in English or French.

Is the YPP examination difficult?

The YPP is competitive and requires preparation. Candidates should become familiar with the examination structure, review relevant materials and practise answering questions under time constraints.

Does passing YPP guarantee a UN job?

No. Successful candidates may be placed on a roster, but roster placement does not guarantee employment.

Is there a fee to apply?

No. The United Nations does not charge an application or examination fee for the YPP.

Final Advice: Start Preparing Now

If you have been dreaming of an international career with purpose, the UN Young Professionals Programme could be an opportunity worth exploring.

With applications expected to open in mid-October, now is the time to prepare.

Don’t wait until the application portal opens.

✅ Check your eligibility
✅ Confirm your nationality and age requirements
✅ Review your degree qualifications
✅ Prepare your supporting documents
✅ Check your English or French proficiency
✅ Learn how the YPP examination works
✅ Review the available preparation materials
✅ Start preparing for the examination

The application may open in October, but your preparation can start today. 🌍🇺🇳

Check the official UN YPP information and prepare ahead of the application opening.

Those interested can apply via Inspira.

To learn more, read the information below, check out our curated series of informative videos about YPP, and continue to visit Important Updates to stay informed!

Source

Information in this article is based on official information published by the United Nations Young Professionals Programme (YPP). Applicants should always consult the latest official UN announcement for the current application cycle, as participating countries, examination subjects, dates and requirements can change.

 

Related Opportunities and Resources

These YPP opportunities are open:

  • ADB Young Professionals Program 2027: Apply for Asian Development Bank Young Professional Jobs in Manila
  • World Bank Young Professionals Program (YPP) 2027: Fully Funded Global Career Opportunity, Eligibility, Application Deadline & How to Apply

You may also find these resources useful:

  • OFY Webinar Series: How to Succeed in Your UN Job Application
  • 5 useful tips for UN interviews: United Nations jobs
  • Insider Tips on Applying to UN Jobs

item.content:encoded:
Are you an experienced practitioner working with networks, coalitions, alliances, partnerships or other collaborative organisations? Collective Mind is inviting practitioners from around the world to become Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows and help co-create a new AI-powered collaboration tool.

The Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows programme 2026–2027 is a year-long opportunity for experienced professionals and practitioners to contribute their knowledge, connect with a global community, influence the development of a new digital tool, and gain free access to the Collective Mind Compass.

Applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis, with the final deadline to participate set for 30 November 2026.

Key Details: Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows 2026–2027

Opportunity Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows
Organisation Collective Mind
Programme Collaboration Fellows
Duration One year
Phase 1 September 2026 – February 2027
Phase 2 March – August 2027
Location Global / Worldwide
Who can apply Experienced collaboration practitioners
Focus areas Strategy, resource mobilisation, MEL and collaboration
Free Compass access Six months from launch
Compass launch February 2027
Application deadline 30 November 2026
Applications Rolling basis

About Collaboration Fellows

Collaboration Fellows are experienced practitioners anywhere in the world who are working in or alongside networks, coalitions, alliances, partnerships, or other collaborative organizations.

The fellowship is a year-long program in two phases:

  1. Co-Creation (September 2026 – February 2027)

During the first phase, Fellows contribute to the knowledge base of our Compass by capturing and sharing their experiences – especially about strategy, resource mobilization, and monitoring, evaluation, and learning – using the templates and tools we provide (e.g., case studies, interviews, guided workflows, etc.).

To be eligible for the second phase, fellows must make at least two contributions during the first Co-Creation phase.

  1. Community Building (March – August 2027)

During the second phase, Fellows gain free access to the Compass, engaging with each other, with our experts, and with other users.

Over the course of the fellowship, fellows will also have opportunities to weigh in on development decisions in meaningful ways, sharing their feedback and ideas on the tool’s design, rollout, and ongoing improvements.

Collaboration Fellows receive multiple benefits:

  • Access: 6 months of free access to the Compass from its launch in February, plus opportunities to extend your access via referrals.
  • Learning and support: Access to resources available on the platform, including the AI coaches, discussions, events, and more.
  • Visibility: Named as a contributor to the tool.
  • Recognition: Contributions may be published, shared, and promoted via Collective Mind’s channels (website, newsletter, LinkedIn).
  • Promotion: Opportunities to be highlighted as an expert, such as during discussions and events.
  • Connections: Connections to diverse global practitioners, including other fellows and Collective Mind’s Co-Creators.
  • Community: Relationship-building via a dedicated shared space for fellows on the platform and fellows-only calls and events.

Collaboration Fellows will also be considered fellows for life, with ongoing opportunities and connection to Collective Mind.

Apply to become a Collective Mind Collaboration Fellow

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The deadline to participate is November 30th.

 

A Fellowship That Continues Beyond 2027

One distinctive feature of the programme is that Collaboration Fellows will be considered fellows for life.

This means participants can remain connected to Collective Mind and potentially benefit from future opportunities, relationships and activities beyond the formal year-long fellowship.

The programme therefore offers more than temporary access to a digital platform. It provides an opportunity to become part of a long-term global community of collaboration practitioners.

How to Apply for the Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows Programme

Interested practitioners are encouraged to apply to join the Collective Mind co-creation effort.

Application deadline: 30 November 2026

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so prospective applicants are encouraged to apply early rather than waiting until the deadline.

Apply to become a Collective Mind Collaboration Fellow

You can also learn more about the Collective Mind Compass and the co-creation initiative through Collective Mind’s official website.

Why Apply?

The Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows programme offers experienced practitioners a chance to shape an emerging AI-powered collaboration tool while sharing their expertise and building connections with a global community.

For professionals working in networks, coalitions, partnerships and collective action, the fellowship could provide a valuable opportunity to contribute practical knowledge, gain visibility, access new learning resources and influence the development of a tool designed to improve collaboration.

Applications are open now and will be reviewed on a rolling basis until 30 November 2026.

Apply for the Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows Programme

Constellation is inviting applications for its 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Intern position, a paid internship designed for university students interested in sustainability, environmental science, business, climate strategy, and the future of clean and reliable energy.

The internship offers students an opportunity to gain practical, hands-on experience with Constellation’s Sustainability Team while contributing to projects connected to sustainability and climate strategy. The position is structured as a remote internship and will run for approximately 10 weeks during the summer of 2027.

For students looking to build professional experience in sustainability, environmental management, climate strategy, clean energy, corporate sustainability, or related areas, this internship provides an opportunity to develop practical skills while working under the supervision of experienced professionals.

About Constellation

Constellation is a major energy company focused on producing clean and reliable electricity and supporting the transition toward a cleaner energy future. The company describes itself as the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the largest producer of clean and reliable energy in the United States.

Following its integration with Calpine, Constellation’s portfolio includes approximately 55 gigawatts of generating capacity across a range of energy sources, including:

  • Nuclear power
  • Natural gas
  • Geothermal energy
  • Hydroelectric power
  • Wind energy
  • Solar energy

According to the opportunity description, this generating capacity is enough to power the equivalent of approximately 27 million homes.

Constellation says its work is guided by a purpose of helping create a cleaner planet and healthier communities while meeting the energy needs of today and tomorrow.

The company’s workplace emphasizes professional growth, learning, collaboration, and meaningful contributions. For interns, this environment can provide exposure to the practical challenges organizations face when developing and implementing sustainability strategies within the energy sector.

About the 2027 Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship

The 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Intern position is intended for highly motivated students pursuing undergraduate or graduate degrees in fields such as Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business Administration, or related disciplines.

The internship is with Constellation’s Sustainability Team and is designed around specific projects that allow interns to gain real-world experience.

Rather than being limited to classroom-based learning, interns will have the opportunity to work on practical assignments under the guidance of an assigned supervisor. This structure can help students understand how sustainability and climate-related concepts are applied in a large energy organization.

The position is listed as:

  • Position: 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Intern
  • Company: Constellation
  • Department/Team: Sustainability Team
  • Job Type: Intern
  • Work Arrangement: Remote
  • Location Listed: Baltimore, Maryland, USA
  • Job Number: 138731
  • Internship Period: June 7, 2027 to August 13, 2027
  • Duration: Approximately 10 weeks
  • Compensation: Paid internship

What Interns Can Expect

The internship is designed to provide students with hands-on professional experience. Interns will be assigned specific projects and will work independently while receiving supervision and guidance.

This type of internship can be particularly valuable for students who want to understand how sustainability functions within a major energy organization.

Through their project work, interns may have opportunities to develop or strengthen skills such as:

  • Sustainability analysis
  • Climate strategy
  • Environmental research
  • Business analysis
  • Problem-solving
  • Written communication
  • Verbal communication
  • Team collaboration
  • Project work
  • Independent working
  • Analytical thinking
  • Creative thinking
  • Professional interpersonal skills

The position also emphasizes the ability to contribute within a team-oriented environment while independently handling assigned responsibilities.

Internship Dates and Duration

The 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship is expected to run for approximately 10 weeks.

The scheduled internship period is:

June 7, 2027 – August 13, 2027

Students considering applying should ensure that they can participate during the stated internship period.

Because the position is specifically described as a summer internship, applicants should also consider how the dates fit with their academic calendar and other commitments.

Educational Requirements

Applicants must currently be pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree.

The preferred areas of study include:

  • Environmental Science
  • Sustainability
  • Business Administration
  • Related fields

Students whose academic programs combine sustainability, environmental studies, climate, business, energy, environmental policy, or other closely related disciplines may find the opportunity particularly relevant.

The requirement to be currently pursuing a degree means the position is targeted toward students rather than applicants who have already completed their education and are seeking a conventional full-time position.

Academic Requirements

Applicants are required to meet specific academic standards.

Constellation lists the following minimum GPA requirements:

  • 2.8 cumulative GPA
  • 3.0 major GPA

In addition to meeting the stated GPA thresholds, candidates should demonstrate a strong overall record of academic performance.

The company specifically seeks candidates with a track record of outstanding academic performance, meaning applicants should be prepared to demonstrate their academic strengths through their application materials.

Students should therefore ensure that their resumes and other application materials accurately present their educational background, academic achievements, relevant coursework, projects, research, or other accomplishments that demonstrate their preparation for the internship.

Skills and Personal Qualities Constellation Is Seeking

Academic qualifications are only one part of the selection criteria. Constellation is also looking for students who can contribute effectively in a professional environment.

Teamwork and Collaboration

Successful interns are expected to be comfortable working in a team-oriented environment. Sustainability and climate strategy projects often involve collaboration between people with different professional backgrounds, so applicants should demonstrate an ability to work effectively with others.

Creative and Analytical Thinking

The internship requires the ability to work both creatively and analytically in a problem-solving environment.

Applicants should therefore be able to approach challenges from different perspectives, analyze information carefully, identify potential solutions, and contribute practical ideas.

Leadership

Constellation also highlights leadership skills among the qualities it seeks. Students do not necessarily need extensive professional management experience; leadership can also be demonstrated through university projects, student organizations, volunteer activities, research, community initiatives, or other experiences where the applicant took responsibility and helped achieve a goal.

Communication Skills

Strong communication is another important requirement.

Applicants should possess:

  • Excellent written communication skills
  • Excellent verbal communication skills
  • Strong interpersonal skills

These abilities are particularly important in a remote working environment, where clear written and verbal communication can help teams coordinate projects and maintain productivity.

Remote Work Opportunity

One of the notable features of this internship is its remote work arrangement.

The position is listed as remote, allowing successful interns to undertake their assigned work without being required to work physically from Constellation’s Baltimore location.

However, applicants should carefully review the company’s employment eligibility requirements before applying. The fact that the internship is remote does not mean it is open to applicants worldwide.

U.S. Work Authorization Requirement

A particularly important requirement for international applicants is Constellation’s visa policy.

The company explicitly states that it will not provide visa sponsorship for this position now or in the future.

Applicants must therefore have the legal ability to work in the United States without requiring either current or future visa sponsorship.

This is an important consideration for international students and candidates living outside the United States. Simply meeting the educational and GPA requirements does not make an applicant eligible if they cannot legally work in the United States under the conditions specified by Constellation.

Prospective applicants should carefully assess their own U.S. work authorization status before submitting an application.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Constellation states that it is an equal opportunity employer.

According to the employer, applicants and employees are considered without regard to characteristics including:

  • Age
  • Color
  • Disability
  • Gender
  • National origin
  • Race
  • Religion
  • Sexual orientation
  • Gender identity
  • Veteran status
  • Other classifications protected under applicable federal, state, or local law

This means the company states that employment decisions are made in accordance with applicable equal employment opportunity requirements.

Constellation also says it is committed to attracting, retaining, and advancing employees who can serve its customers, partners, and communities while maintaining a workplace based on mutual respect and opportunities for professional growth.

Disability and Interview Accommodations

Applicants who have a disability, whether visible or invisible, and require an accommodation to complete the application process can contact Constellation’s Talent Acquisition team using the accommodation contact provided in the original listing.

Candidates who require an interview accommodation can also use the company’s interview accommodation resources.

Applicants should request accommodations through the appropriate company channel if they need assistance during the recruitment process.

Nuclear Site Access and Identification Requirements

Constellation notes that many of its roles may require unescorted entry and access to nuclear sites at the time of hire and during employment.

The company states that, beginning May 7, 2025, candidates requiring unescorted access to applicable nuclear sites need an acceptable form of identification in accordance with the REAL ID Act.

The identification options listed include:

  • REAL ID
  • Passport
  • Visa
  • TWIC Card

This requirement may not necessarily apply to every intern or to a fully remote position, but applicants should be aware that Constellation operates nuclear facilities and that certain roles may involve additional access requirements.

Why This Internship Could Be Valuable

The Constellation Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship can be valuable for students seeking to establish a career in the growing sustainability and clean-energy sector.

1. Paid Professional Experience

The internship is a paid summer opportunity, allowing students to gain professional experience while receiving compensation.

2. Experience With a Major Energy Company

Working with a large energy organization can expose students to the scale and complexity of sustainability challenges within the power sector.

3. Hands-On Project Experience

Interns will work on specific projects rather than simply observing the Sustainability Team. This can help them build practical experience that may strengthen future applications for graduate programs, internships, fellowships, and entry-level sustainability positions.

4. Remote Working Experience

The remote structure can help students develop the communication, organization, independence, and collaboration skills required in modern professional workplaces.

5. Sustainability and Climate Exposure

Students interested in sustainability, climate strategy, environmental issues, and energy transition can gain exposure to these subjects within a major energy organization.

6. Professional Development

Working under an assigned supervisor can give interns the opportunity to receive guidance while learning how professional teams plan, execute, and deliver projects.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Students interested in this opportunity should make sure their application clearly demonstrates both their academic qualifications and relevant skills.

A strong application should emphasize:

  1. Current degree program: Clearly state the degree being pursued and the institution.
  2. Relevant academic field: Highlight Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business Administration, or another related discipline.
  3. GPA: Make sure the application reflects the required cumulative and major GPA where appropriate.
  4. Relevant coursework: Include courses connected to sustainability, environmental management, climate, business, energy, data analysis, or related subjects.
  5. Projects: Highlight university, research, community, or personal projects relevant to sustainability or climate strategy.
  6. Communication: Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication abilities.
  7. Problem-solving: Provide examples of analytical or creative approaches used to solve problems.
  8. Leadership: Mention experiences where you led or took responsibility for a project or activity.
  9. Teamwork: Highlight successful collaboration with classmates, colleagues, organizations, or project teams.
  10. Remote-work readiness: Where relevant, demonstrate your ability to work independently, manage deadlines, and communicate effectively in a remote environment.

Applicants should also carefully review their resume for spelling, formatting, consistency, and relevance before submitting it.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly suited to students who are currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in:

  • Environmental Science
  • Sustainability
  • Business Administration
  • A related field

Applicants should also meet the required GPA thresholds, demonstrate strong academic performance, possess effective communication and interpersonal skills, and be capable of contributing creatively and analytically to problem-solving activities.

The internship may be especially relevant to students planning careers in:

  • Sustainability
  • Climate strategy
  • Environmental management
  • Clean energy
  • Energy policy
  • Corporate sustainability
  • Environmental consulting
  • Sustainable business
  • Climate risk
  • Energy transition
  • Environmental research

APPLY HERE

Geographic and Nationality Eligibility

Although the internship is remote, it is not presented as a worldwide remote opportunity.

Constellation requires applicants to have the ability to lawfully work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship.

Therefore, applicants from outside the United States should not assume that they are eligible simply because the position is remote. Eligibility depends on the applicant’s existing legal authorization to work in the United States and the employer’s stated sponsorship policy.

Constellation’s equal opportunity statement also indicates that employment consideration is not restricted on the basis of race, national origin, or other protected characteristics. However, the U.S. work authorization requirement remains applicable.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Constellation Energy 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship.

Application Process

Interested candidates should apply through Constellation’s official careers/application system.

Applicants should prepare their application carefully and make sure that all information provided is accurate. Particular attention should be given to degree status, field of study, GPA, work authorization, and relevant academic or professional experience.

Candidates should also be cautious about recruitment scams and rely on Constellation’s official careers channels when submitting personal information or application materials.

Deadline

No specific application deadline is stated in the provided job listing.

Because the position is for Summer 2027, interested students should consider applying as early as possible rather than waiting for a deadline to be announced or for the position to close.

Key Details at a Glance

  • Opportunity: 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Intern
  • Organization: Constellation
  • Opportunity Type: Paid internship
  • Work Arrangement: Remote
  • Listed Location: Baltimore, Maryland, USA
  • Internship Duration: Approximately 10 weeks
  • Start Date: June 7, 2027
  • End Date: August 13, 2027
  • Eligible Education: Students pursuing Bachelor’s or Master’s degrees
  • Preferred Fields: Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business Administration, or related fields
  • Minimum Cumulative GPA: 2.8
  • Minimum Major GPA: 3.0
  • Work Authorization: Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship
  • Visa Sponsorship: Not provided
  • Application Deadline: Not specified in the provided listing

Conclusion

The Constellation 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship presents a valuable opportunity for students who want to gain practical experience at the intersection of sustainability, climate strategy, business, and the energy sector.

The approximately 10-week paid internship is structured around hands-on projects within Constellation’s Sustainability Team, giving successful candidates an opportunity to develop professional skills while working under an assigned supervisor. The position particularly targets students pursuing Bachelor’s or Master’s degrees in Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business Administration, and related disciplines.

Applicants should pay close attention to the 2.8 cumulative GPA and 3.0 major GPA requirements, as well as the requirement to be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship. Although the position is remote, it should not be interpreted as an opportunity open to candidates worldwide without U.S. work authorization.

For qualified students seeking to build experience in sustainability and climate strategy, this internship can be a strong opportunity to gain practical project experience and develop skills relevant to the rapidly evolving clean-energy and sustainability sector.

item.content:encoded:
Women pursuing careers in diplomacy, international relations, foreign policy, security, human rights, global development, and other related areas have an opportunity to join the Women in Foreign Affairs Network Mentorship Group, an initiative designed to create a supportive and inclusive environment where women can learn from experienced leaders in foreign affairs.

The 16th Cohort of the Women in Foreign Affairs Network Mentorship Group will be led by Alyse Nelson, President, CEO, and Co-Founder of Vital Voices Global Partnership. The mentorship group will provide participants with an opportunity to engage in three monthly, off-the-record group coaching sessions focused on leadership, decision-making, navigating professional challenges, and gaining behind-the-scenes insights into the foreign policy field.

Applications for the 2026 mentorship group are currently open, with applications due by October 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST.

About the Women in Foreign Affairs Mentorship Group

The Women in Foreign Affairs Network Mentorship Group seeks to bring together women from diverse professional and personal backgrounds who share an interest in foreign affairs and want to learn from established women leaders.

The program is designed around the idea that women working in foreign policy and international affairs can benefit significantly from a supportive professional community. Participants will have the opportunity to learn directly from prominent leaders while also connecting with other women navigating careers in the field.

Rather than focusing solely on formal instruction, the mentorship group emphasizes practical insights and candid conversations. The sessions are held off the record, creating an environment where participants can engage openly and discuss issues that may not typically be addressed in public professional settings.

The mentorship group is intended to help women better understand the realities of leadership and professional advancement in foreign affairs while developing relationships with peers and senior figures in the field.

What Participants Can Expect

Selected participants will take part in three monthly group coaching sessions led by the cohort’s mentor.

Each mentor is responsible for selecting a particular theme and guiding participants through a series of three sessions focused on that theme. The sessions are intended to provide practical and behind-the-scenes perspectives on leadership and professional development.

Participants can expect discussions covering areas such as

  • Challenges commonly faced by women in the foreign policy and foreign affairs sector.
  • Leadership approaches and decision-making processes.
  • Professional challenges and how experienced leaders navigate them.
  • Blind spots and structural challenges within the foreign affairs field.
  • Career decision-making and professional growth.
  • Leadership development and building confidence.
  • Perspectives gained from years of experience in international affairs.
  • Building relationships with other women working across the foreign affairs ecosystem.

The off-the-record format is particularly important because it is intended to provide a safe environment for participants to ask questions, share experiences, and engage in honest discussions.

Attendance Requirement

Participation in the mentorship group requires a meaningful commitment from selected candidates.

The organizers have stated that at least two of the three sessions are mandatory. Applicants must therefore confirm that they are available for the scheduled sessions before applying.

The three sessions are scheduled as follows:

Session 1

Date: October 15, 2026
Time: 7:00–8:00 PM CEST / 1:00–2:00 PM EST

Session 2

Date: November 6, 2026
Time: 7:00–8:00 PM CEST / 1:00–2:00 PM EST

Session 3

Date: December 9, 2026
Time: 8:00–9:00 PM CEST / 2:00–3:00 PM EST

Applicants must confirm their availability and understand that they are required to attend at least two of these meetings.

Goals of the Women in Foreign Affairs Network Mentorship Group

The mentorship group has several overarching goals aimed at strengthening women’s participation and leadership in foreign affairs.

1. Building an Intergenerational Community of Women Leaders

One of the central objectives is to connect women at different stages of their professional journeys.

By bringing together women with varying levels of experience, the network seeks to encourage knowledge sharing, mentorship, collaboration, and professional relationships across generations.

2. Making Foreign Affairs More Accessible and Inclusive

Foreign affairs can be a highly competitive and complex professional field. The program aims to make the sector more accessible by providing women with opportunities to learn directly from experienced professionals and understand how careers in foreign affairs develop.

3. Providing Behind-the-Scenes Leadership Insights

Traditional professional development programs often focus on formal qualifications and technical knowledge. This mentorship group goes further by creating opportunities to learn about the practical realities of leadership.

Participants can gain insights into how experienced leaders approach difficult decisions, navigate professional challenges, and develop their careers.

4. Creating a Safe Space for Career Conversations

The network seeks to provide an environment where women can support one another in making professional and career decisions.

Because the sessions are off the record, participants are encouraged to engage in open conversations and learn from both mentors and peers.

About the Q4 2026 Mentor: Alyse Nelson

The 16th Cohort will be led by Alyse Nelson, a prominent leader in women’s leadership, international affairs, and global development.

Nelson is the President, CEO, and Co-Founder of Vital Voices Global Partnership, an organization focused on investing in women leaders working to address major global challenges.

Vital Voices works across areas including:

  • Economic empowerment.
  • Women’s political participation.
  • Human rights.
  • Women’s leadership.
  • Global development and social impact.

Under Nelson’s leadership, Vital Voices has grown to directly serve more than 47,000 women across 188 countries and territories, giving her extensive experience working with women leaders and organizations across the world.

Her professional background also includes significant experience within U.S. foreign policy.

Previously, Nelson served as Deputy Director of the Vital Voices Global Democracy Initiative at the U.S. Department of State. In that role, she helped advance women’s leadership as a U.S. foreign policy objective while working alongside former First Lady Hillary Clinton and former Secretary of State Madeleine Albright.

Her experience therefore spans government, international affairs, women’s leadership, diplomacy, civil society, and global development.

Nelson has also been featured by major international media organizations and publications, including The Washington Post, Financial Times, The Wall Street Journal, Reuters, BBC, CNN, and NPR.

She is a Member of the Council on Foreign Relations and received the 2022 David Rockefeller Bridging Leadership Award.

Her extensive experience makes the Q4 2026 mentorship group particularly relevant for women seeking practical perspectives on leadership, foreign policy, international affairs, and advancing women’s participation in global decision-making.

Who Can Apply?

The Women in Foreign Affairs Mentorship Group is looking for women with a range of professional experience and a passion for foreign affairs.

The minimum academic requirement is a Bachelor’s degree.

The program is therefore potentially relevant to women who have already established careers as well as those who are at earlier stages of their professional development.

Applicants may have backgrounds or professional interests connected to areas such as:

  • Diplomacy.
  • Security and defense policy.
  • Human rights and humanitarian issues.
  • International law.
  • Global environmental and climate policy.
  • Global economic policy.
  • Global health policy.
  • Global gender policy.
  • Technology and foreign policy.
  • Regional specialization.
  • Other areas related to foreign affairs.

The application allows candidates to select up to three areas of expertise or provide another relevant area under the “Other” option.

Areas of Expertise Covered in the Application

Applicants are asked to identify their area of expertise. The available areas include:

Diplomacy

Applicants working in diplomatic affairs, international relations, diplomatic engagement, foreign missions, or related areas may identify diplomacy as their area of expertise.

Security and Defense Policy

This category is relevant to professionals working on national security, international security, defense policy, conflict prevention, peace and security, or related issues.

Human Rights and Humanitarian Issues

Women working in human rights, humanitarian response, protection, international development, refugee affairs, or related fields may select this area.

International Law

Applicants with expertise in international legal affairs, international treaties, human rights law, humanitarian law, or related areas can identify international law.

Global Environmental and Climate Policy

This area is relevant to professionals working on climate change, environmental policy, sustainability, natural resources, or international environmental governance.

Global Economic Policy

Applicants working on international economics, trade, development finance, economic policy, global markets, or related fields may select this category.

Global Health Policy

Professionals working on international health, global health governance, health policy, health security, or related issues may select global health policy.

Global Gender Policy

This category may be particularly relevant to applicants working on gender equality, women’s empowerment, women’s political participation, gender policy, or related international issues.

Technology and Foreign Policy

Applicants working at the intersection of technology and international affairs can identify this as their area of expertise.

Regional Specialization

Candidates with professional or academic expertise focused on a particular geographical region can select regional specialization.

Other

Applicants whose expertise does not fall into the listed categories may specify another relevant area.

Application Requirements

The application requires candidates to provide several pieces of personal and professional information.

Applicants will be asked to provide:

  1. Full name
  2. Email address
  3. LinkedIn profile
  4. City of residence for the next six months
  5. Area of expertise
  6. Background and explanation of why the program matters to them
  7. Additional information they would like the organizers to know
  8. Confirmation of availability for the mentorship sessions

The application includes a 250-word maximum for the question asking candidates to explain their background and why the program matters to them.

There is also an optional section allowing applicants to share additional information, with a 100-word maximum.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because the mentorship group is likely to receive more applications than available places, candidates should make their application focused and compelling.

A strong application should clearly demonstrate the connection between the applicant’s professional or academic background and foreign affairs.

Applicants should consider highlighting:

  • Their professional experience in foreign affairs or a related field.
  • Their academic background and relevant areas of study.
  • Their specific interest in international affairs.
  • The challenges they have encountered in their career.
  • Their leadership ambitions.
  • How mentorship would contribute to their professional development.
  • Why learning from an experienced foreign affairs leader would be valuable to them.
  • What perspectives or experiences they could contribute to the mentorship community.
  • Their commitment to supporting other women in the field.

The 250-word response should not simply repeat information from a CV. Instead, applicants should use the limited space to tell a clear professional story and explain why participation in the mentorship group is important at this stage of their career.

Important Dates and Application Timeline

Applicants should take note of the following dates:

Application deadline: October 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST

Selected candidates notified: No later than October 5, 2026

First mentorship session: October 15, 2026

Second mentorship session: November 6, 2026

Third mentorship session: December 9, 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours, particularly because the organizers have indicated that there may not be sufficient space for everyone who applies.

APPLY HERE

What Happens After the Application?

Following the application deadline, selected candidates will be notified by email.

The organizers have indicated that candidates selected for the cohort will be informed no later than October 5, 2026.

Applicants who are not selected for this particular cohort should not necessarily consider the process the end of their engagement with the network. The organizers have stated that they intend to keep applicants informed about registration opportunities for upcoming cohorts.

This means that applying can potentially provide an opportunity to remain connected to future mentorship opportunities offered through the network.

Why This Mentorship Opportunity Matters

Women continue to play an increasingly important role in diplomacy, international development, foreign policy, global governance, peace and security, humanitarian affairs, and other areas of international cooperation.

However, professional advancement in these sectors can involve challenges that are not always addressed through academic qualifications alone.

Mentorship can help professionals understand the informal dimensions of leadership, including how experienced leaders make decisions, build professional relationships, navigate institutions, handle difficult situations, and identify opportunities for advancement.

The Women in Foreign Affairs Mentorship Group is designed around this type of practical learning.

Its emphasis on candid, off-the-record conversations can also allow participants to gain perspectives that may be difficult to obtain through conventional courses, conferences, or formal training programs.

A Valuable Opportunity for Women in International Affairs

The mentorship group can be particularly valuable for women who want to strengthen their careers in areas where international policy, diplomacy, leadership, and global decision-making intersect.

Participants will not only have the opportunity to learn from Alyse Nelson but can also become part of an intergenerational community of women working across different areas of foreign affairs.

The diversity of expertise represented in the application process means that the cohort may bring together professionals working in diplomacy, security, humanitarian affairs, climate policy, economics, global health, gender policy, technology, international law, and regional affairs.

Such a community can create opportunities for peer learning and long-term professional relationships.

Visit HERE for more information about the Women in Foreign Affairs Mentorship Group 2026 with Alyse Nelson.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Women in Foreign Affairs Mentorship Group?

It is a mentorship and group coaching initiative of the Women in Foreign Affairs Network that connects women interested in foreign affairs with experienced leaders for practical discussions on leadership, career development, decision-making, and challenges within the field.

Who is the Q4 2026 mentor?

The 16th Cohort will be led by Alyse Nelson, President, CEO, and Co-Founder of Vital Voices Global Partnership.

How many sessions are included?

The mentorship group consists of three monthly off-the-record group coaching sessions.

Is attendance mandatory?

Yes. Participants are required to attend at least two of the three sessions.

What is the minimum academic qualification?

Applicants must have at least a Bachelor’s degree.

Do applicants need to have extensive professional experience?

No specific number of years of professional experience is stated. The organizers are looking for women with a range of professional experience and a passion for foreign affairs.

When is the application deadline?

Applications must be submitted by October 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST.

When will selected candidates be notified?

Selected candidates will be informed by email no later than October 5, 2026.

What if I am not selected?

The organizers indicate that they will keep applicants informed about registration for upcoming cohorts, meaning applicants may have opportunities to participate in future mentorship groups.

Conclusion

The Women in Foreign Affairs Network Mentorship Group 2026 presents an opportunity for women interested in foreign affairs to learn directly from an experienced global leader while joining a community of women working across different areas of international affairs.

The 16th Cohort, led by Alyse Nelson, offers three off-the-record group coaching sessions focused on leadership, decision-making, professional challenges, and the realities of navigating the foreign policy field. Nelson’s experience leading Vital Voices Global Partnership and her previous work at the U.S. Department of State provide a strong foundation for practical conversations about women’s leadership and international affairs.

Women with at least a Bachelor’s degree and a passion for foreign affairs are encouraged to consider applying. Candidates should carefully prepare their background statement, clearly explain why the mentorship matters to their professional journey, and ensure they can attend at least two of the three scheduled sessions.

The application deadline is October 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST. Since the organizers expect that there may be more applicants than available places, interested candidates should submit a thoughtful application before the deadline.

For women seeking to expand their understanding of foreign affairs, strengthen their leadership capabilities, and build relationships with other women in the field, this mentorship group provides a valuable opportunity for professional learning and community building.

For more global Fellowship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.
