item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Field Studies Council Youth Panel 2026, an exciting opportunity for young people in the United Kingdom to contribute their ideas, experiences and perspectives to one of the UK’s leading environmental education charities.

The Youth Panel brings together young people who are passionate about nature, the outdoors and environmental education. Panel members have the opportunity to influence how the Field Studies Council engages with young people, participate in discussions with staff and trustees, develop valuable transferable skills, meet other young naturalists and environmentalists, and contribute to content and projects focused on youth engagement.

Applications opened on 14 September 2026, and eligible young people are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline of 9:00 pm on Sunday, 27 September 2026.

About the Field Studies Council Youth Panel

The Field Studies Council Youth Panel is a UK-wide group of young people that helps shape nature education and youth engagement through strategic insight and feedback.

Youth Panel members play an important role within the Field Studies Council by bringing young people’s perspectives into organisational discussions. Rather than simply participating in environmental activities, members can contribute their views on how young people can be better engaged with nature, outdoor learning and environmental education.

The opportunity is particularly suitable for young people who want to become a stronger voice for their generation while gaining practical experience in communication, decision-making, teamwork and influencing.

The role is voluntary, meaning that successful applicants will not be employed or paid as Youth Panel members. However, the position provides opportunities for personal development, networking, training and involvement in the work of the Field Studies Council.

What Does a Youth Panel Member Do?

Youth Panel members are expected to actively contribute to the Panel and participate in activities that support the Field Studies Council’s youth engagement work.

The Panel provides young people with an opportunity to have their voices heard in discussions concerning the organisation’s provision for young people. Members can provide feedback, share ideas, participate in meetings and contribute to projects based on their interests and skills.

The Field Studies Council describes its Youth Panel members as key members of the organisation who can engage in high-level discussions about its provision for young people.

This makes the opportunity particularly valuable for young people interested in:

  • Environmental education
  • Nature and conservation
  • Youth engagement
  • Environmental leadership
  • Communication and content creation
  • Decision-making
  • Advocacy and representation
  • Biodiversity
  • Outdoor learning
  • Community engagement
  • Developing leadership and teamwork skills

Key Benefits of Joining the Youth Panel

Being selected for the Field Studies Council Youth Panel can provide a combination of environmental, leadership, communication and personal-development experiences.

1. Participate in a Funded Residential Weekend

Youth Panel members will have the opportunity to attend a funded residential weekend at a Field Studies Council field centre in the UK.

For the 2026 intake, the residential weekend is scheduled to take place from Friday 6 November to Sunday 8 November 2026 at Preston Montford, Shropshire. The costs associated with the residential are covered.

This residential experience provides an opportunity for members to meet other participants in person and take part in Youth Panel activities.

2. Access Training Opportunities

Youth Panel members can participate in training opportunities during their time on the Panel.

These include heavily subsidised Biodiversity Courses, which may be offered online and in person. Such opportunities can help young people expand their understanding of biodiversity and develop knowledge that complements their interest in nature and the environment.

3. Network With Other Young Environmentalists

The Youth Panel provides an opportunity to meet other young people who are passionate about nature.

Throughout their term, members will have opportunities to connect with other young naturalists and environmentalists. This can create opportunities for collaboration, knowledge exchange and building relationships with peers who share similar interests.

4. Develop Transferable Skills

One of the important benefits of the Youth Panel is the opportunity to develop practical skills that can be useful beyond environmental activities.

The Field Studies Council specifically identifies skills such as:

  • Meeting skills
  • Decision-making
  • Influencing
  • Collaboration
  • Communication
  • Participation in organisational discussions

These experiences can be valuable for young people who are considering future education, volunteering, employment or leadership opportunities.

5. Create Content for Social Media and Blogs

Youth Panel members can also contribute to communications activities.

Members may have opportunities to create content for social media and blogs that can be shared through Field Studies Council channels as well as through their own channels.

This element of the role may be particularly useful for young people interested in digital communication, journalism, social media, content creation, environmental storytelling or public engagement.

6. Represent Young People in Decision-Making

Youth Panel members can represent young people’s perspectives in decision-making meetings involving Field Studies Council staff and trustees.

They may also have opportunities to represent the Field Studies Council at events or conferences.

This provides participants with exposure to organisational decision-making and gives them an opportunity to contribute directly to conversations concerning young people and environmental education.

Duration of the Youth Panel Role

Members recruited during autumn 2026 are expected to serve on the Youth Panel for two years.

The role is voluntary, and successful applicants will therefore need to be prepared to make a sustained commitment to the Panel throughout this period.

A two-year commitment can allow members to build meaningful experience over time rather than participating in a one-off activity. It also gives participants the opportunity to develop their skills and contribute to projects throughout their period of service.

Meetings and Time Commitment

Youth Panel members participate in both online and in-person activities.

The Panel holds an in-person residential once a year at a Field Studies Council centre. For the 2026 cohort, the annual residential is scheduled for 6–8 November 2026 at Preston Montford. Applicants are expected to confirm their availability for this date.

In addition, monthly online meetings are held. These meetings alternate between weekday evenings and generally take place on Mondays, Wednesdays or Thursdays from 6:00 pm to 7:15 pm.

The Field Studies Council recognises that young people may require greater flexibility at certain times of the year.

Youth Panel members are expected to attend a minimum of four meetings per year and contribute to associated tasks and projects.

This means applicants should consider their existing commitments, including school and other activities, before applying.

The opportunity is open to young people who meet the specific requirements set by the Field Studies Council.

Applicants must:

  • Be aged between 16 and 18 at the time of applying.
  • Be based in the United Kingdom.
  • Be able to attend the in-person Youth Panel residential from Friday 6 November to Sunday 8 November 2026 at Preston Montford, Shropshire.
  • Be able to commit approximately a couple of hours per month to meetings and related tasks.

The Field Studies Council states that it welcomes applications from young people regardless of their experience or background.

It also indicates that it is particularly interested in representatives from Scotland and Wales, while the Youth Panel itself is UK-wide.

Country and Continent Eligibility

The opportunity is restricted geographically to young people based in the United Kingdom.

Therefore, applicants from the following UK nations can potentially apply, provided they meet the other requirements:

  • England
  • Scotland
  • Wales
  • Northern Ireland

The source specifically highlights Scotland and Wales as areas from which the Field Studies Council is especially keen to receive representation.

The eligible continent is Europe, but the actual eligibility requirement is more specific: applicants must be based in the UK. The opportunity is not presented as open to applicants from Europe generally.

No Previous Experience Is Required

An important feature of the opportunity is that applicants do not need to demonstrate extensive previous experience.

The Field Studies Council welcomes applications from young people regardless of their experience or background.

This means applicants should not assume that they need an extensive environmental, conservation or leadership record to be considered. Instead, they should use their application to explain who they are, what motivates them, what they hope to learn and what they can contribute to the Panel.

What Is Required in the Application?

The application consists of three main questions designed to help the Field Studies Council understand applicants, their motivations and the contribution they could make to youth engagement.

Question 1: Tell Us About Yourself and Your Motivation

Applicants are asked to explain something about themselves, their experiences and what motivates them to join the Field Studies Council Youth Panel.

The maximum response length is 200 words.

Applicants may consider discussing:

  • Their connection with the outdoors
  • Previous volunteering roles
  • Areas they would like to become involved in
  • Their motivation for representing young people
  • Their interest in the Field Studies Council

The organisation is looking for insight into the applicant as an individual and an understanding of why they want to become part of the Youth Panel.

Question 2: What Do You Hope to Learn?

The second question asks applicants to explain what they hope to learn from participating in the role.

The maximum response length is 200 words.

Applicants can consider discussing:

  • Skills they want to develop
  • What excites them about joining the Youth Panel
  • How the opportunity could support their future
  • Personal or professional development goals

This is an opportunity for applicants to demonstrate that they have thought about how Youth Panel participation could contribute to their growth.

Question 3: What Can You Bring to the Panel?

The third question asks applicants what they could contribute to the Panel and what they hope to achieve as a Panel member.

The maximum response length is 300 words.

Applicants can discuss:

  • Particular skills they possess
  • Relevant experiences
  • What distinguishes them from other applicants
  • Ideas they could contribute
  • Their goals as a Youth Panel member
  • How they would balance Panel responsibilities with school and other commitments

This question is particularly important because it allows applicants to demonstrate both their potential contribution and their understanding of the responsibilities involved in joining the Panel.

Application Tips

The Field Studies Council recommends preparing responses in Microsoft Word or Google Docs before copying and pasting them into the online application form.

This approach can make it easier for applicants to draft, edit and review their answers before submitting the application.

Applicants should ensure that their responses directly answer each question while remaining within the specified word limits.

Young people should also consider demonstrating genuine motivation rather than simply listing achievements. Since the Field Studies Council welcomes applicants regardless of their experience or background, applicants can focus on their interests, perspectives, aspirations and willingness to contribute.

Alternative Application Format for Applicants Who Find Online Forms Difficult

The Field Studies Council provides an alternative way to respond to the application questions.

Applicants who find completing online forms difficult and would prefer to talk through their answers can record their responses in video or audio format.

Each question can be answered in a recording of up to three minutes.

Applicants choosing this option are instructed to email their files to youth.engagement@field-studies-council.org.

This provides an alternative route for young people who may communicate their ideas more effectively through spoken responses.
